domain_title: Models, agents, providers, tools and supply chain
title: Provider, vendor and contractual governance
canonical_definition: Third-party AI services are evaluated, contractually governed, monitored and replaceable in the context of the actual system.

conditions: Systems using third-party models, hosting, tools, data services, evaluators or managed AI components.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Are provider terms, data practices, subprocessors, service limits, audit rights and exit needs defined?
Are contractual controls, approved configurations, monitoring and contingency arrangements implemented?
Does current evidence show that material provider changes and service failures are detected, assessed and acted upon?

capability_indicators: Retention and training use are confirmed

conditions: Refer a material failure of provider, vendor and contractual governance to the accountable authority before a consequential transition.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, GOVERN 6.1 (PDF p. 29), GOVERN 6.2 (PDF p. 29), MANAGE 3.1 (PDF p. 37)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on third-party risk policies, contingency and monitoring. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

governance_purpose: Make provider, vendor and contractual governance verifiable against the current AI system, decision context and accountable ownership.
distinct_claim: C4 evaluates provider, vendor and contractual governance using evidence from intent through operation. AP-C4 independently assesses evidence of vendor assurance substitution.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: The versioned definition identifies provider terms, subprocessors, usage and data settings, service obligations, audit access and exit requirements. Record the accountable owner, scope and material assumptions.

The current release demonstrates configuration and contract controls reconciled with the integrated service plus provider change monitoring and an exit route. Trace the decisions and controls to attributable records.

Representative, executed evidence provides dated provider-change or outage exercise tying notice, impact review, fallback and accountable decision to the integrated service. Compare expected and observed outcomes and record exceptions.
For an operating system, current records cover the material paths involved in provider, vendor and contractual governance, including relevant exceptions and changes.

required_evidence.title: Versioned scope and control definition
required_evidence.description: Provide provider terms, subprocessors, usage and data settings, service obligations, audit access and exit requirements. Include the affected workflow, current version and accountable owner.

required_evidence.title: Effective implementation records
required_evidence.description: Demonstrate configuration and contract controls reconciled with the integrated service plus provider change monitoring and an exit route. Trace the scope, control and authority to the current implementation, including exceptions.

required_evidence.title: Representative verification results
required_evidence.description: Provide dated provider-change or outage exercise tying notice, impact review, fallback and accountable decision to the integrated service. Include current version, test scope, criteria, expected and observed outcomes, and unresolved failures.

required_evidence.title: Current operating or change evidence
required_evidence.description: Retain dated records that show how provider, vendor and contractual governance works for the assessed scope, including the relevant exceptions and any material change since the evidence was captured.

sufficiency: Start with provider terms, subprocessors, usage and data settings, service obligations, audit access and exit requirements. Reconcile it against the effective controls and representative results for the same operating scope and version.

Use dated provider-change or outage exercise tying notice, impact review, fallback and accountable decision to the integrated service to support effectiveness at the relevant lifecycle stage. Record missing paths and unresolved conflicts as UNKNOWN. A verified shortfall can support a gap without resolving the other questions.
Reassess affected evidence after a material change. An accountable human validates or approves the result where required by the lifecycle target.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A specification supports DECLARED intent. Effective implementation records may support IMPLEMENTED. Representative executed tests support TESTED within their scope. Current operating evidence supports OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED for covered paths and time. Record human assurance independently.
false_positive_guards: A provider attestation can support a narrowly identified dependency claim within its verified scope.
Reconcile document claims with the effective release, actual operation and relevant exceptions before recording satisfaction.
prohibited_inferences: A capability gap alone cannot establish AP-C4 presence.
An approved design or evidence plan cannot establish test execution or operational effectiveness.
Satisfying this capability cannot by itself authorize progression or establish legal compliance.

finding_definitions.title: Material definition or intent gap in provider, vendor and contractual governance
Verified implementation or effectiveness gap in provider, vendor and contractual governance
Evidence remains insufficient for provider, vendor and contractual governance in the assessed scope
